chapter: The Dew Drop, Blue Eagle and visiting stars
title: The Dew Drop hotel and stranded artists
summary: Frank's hotel housed James Brown, and Chuck Willis's saxophonist stayed behind.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah. a lot of them big names that came in town, not only in New Orleans, but all the surrounding area. So you could hold the hill with book things, Senator Frank, Frank would book things, Senator Tom Couch, you know, so it was like around, and Frank had a nightclub plus a hotel. So the entertainer would come in town and play for him, and they would most likely stay in this hotel for nothing. So people had the chance to follow. As an example, Jan Brown came in town before he got big, he stayed at the Dew Drop about three or four weeks stranded. And you know, this is how people got to know Jan Brown, because he came out here with the Four Flames, see, Jan Brown and the Four Flames, before the band, it was a quartet, and he got stranded down here. Chuck Willis, Chuck Willis came by, he stayed at the Dew Drop, and he left the saxophone player, and he had never went back to Cincinnati. Nose, Nose was working at Wehrlein. Nose never did go back to Rufus Gore. Rufus Gore, never did go back to Cincinnati, where he was from, stayed here in North. And I remember the weekend when Chuck Willis was here, and that Monday I was going to Baton Rouge to play at the Purple Circle for Frank Pena, and he told me, take that saxophone player, he can play good. And I brought, that's how I met Nose. The first Monday night he stayed, he went to Baton Rouge with us. And that's when I got to know what kind of fella he was. Yeah, Trevor, yeah.
